description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", spans from 40% to 65% and is linearly scaled. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with solid circles, starting at approximately 40% accuracy and rising to about 45%. The "MEND" method, shown as a brown line with diamond markers, begins near 45% and increases to about 57%. The "FT" method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at roughly 40% and rises to approximately 48%. The "MEMIT" method, indicated by a purple line with star markers, begins near 45% and increases to about 55%. The "IKE" method, shown as a red line with triangle markers, starts at approximately 43% and rises to about 50%. The "ROME" method, represented by a green line with square markers, begins at about 51% and increases to approximately 66%. All lines show a general upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy and Base the lowest.
